<div class="note-box">

**Where this sits.** Round 6 produced an M2 table headlined "MELD-λ1 beats
every single-population candidate" — a result that motivated keeping the
between-population B term. Round 6b is the diagnostic that puts that
headline under six controls (D1–D6) and finds it does not survive. The M1
result from Round 6 (B distorts the LD matrix more than population choice
does) stands; the M2 result needed the diagnostics to become interpretable.
This is the round that fixes the analysis rather than the round that
extends it.

</div>

***

# Question

Under what conditions is the Round 6 M2 headline (MELD-λ1 > single-pop)
actually testing a property of the between-population term B, versus a
property of numerical conditioning or an unfair reference set? Six
diagnostics were named a priori:

- **D1** — put MELD-λ0 (the missing candidate) back in the M2 table.
- **D2** — apply uniform PSD repair to every candidate before scoring.
- **D3** — a permuted-ΔAF placebo B; if it reproduces the MELD-λ1 advantage,
  the "B is what predicts" story is falsified.
- **D4** — a λ sweep from 0 to 1 in fine steps; if the picture is
  monotone-in-λ post-repair, B carries real signal.
- **D5** — stratify (M2\_λ=1 − M2\_λ=0) by |ΔAF| tertile; a real B signal
  should concentrate where the derivation says it should.
- **D6** — block-bootstrap 95 % CIs on everything; the Round 6 SD-based
  error bars were too tight.

Chr22 only (24 blocks), all candidates including MELD-λ0,
`w_eur ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}`.

***

# D1 — MELD-λ0 in M2 (the missing candidate)

Pre-repair r² at δ = 0.01, size-weighted mean across chr22 blocks:

| candidate     | w = 0.25 | w = 0.50 | w = 0.75 |
| ---           | ---:     | ---:     | ---:     |
| MELD-λ0       | 0.62     | 0.68     | 0.84     |
| MELD-λ1       | 0.62     | 0.73     | 0.84     |
| MELD-pooled   | —        | 0.72     | —        |
| EUR           | 0.39     | 0.47     | 0.62     |
| AFR           | 0.48     | 0.47     | 0.46     |

MELD-λ0 tracks MELD-λ1 exactly at w = 0.25 and w = 0.75 even *pre-repair*.
The 0.05 gap at w = 0.5 is the only place where "λ1 wins" has visible
support in pre-repair scores — and D2 removes it.

***

# D2 — Uniform PSD repair (eigen-clamp + diag rescale)

Every candidate matrix is passed through the same eigen-clamp
`eigen(R); λ ← max(λ, 0); reconstruct; rescale diagonal to 1` before the
masked-z solve. This equalises numerical conditioning across candidates.

Pre-repair minimum eigenvalue (median across chr22 blocks) shows the
conditioning gradient the diagnostics prompt predicted:

| candidate    | median min-eig (any w) |
| ---          | ---:                    |
| MELD-λ1      | −0.038 to −0.044        |
| MELD-λ0      | −0.045 to −0.051        |
| AFR          | −0.063                  |
| MELD-pooled  | −0.065                  |
| EUR          | −0.096                  |

Better-conditioned candidates (less negative min-eig) score higher M2
pre-repair. Spearman between median pre-repair min-eig and pre-repair M2
across candidates: w = 0.25 ρ = +1.00; w = 0.50 ρ = +0.30; w = 0.75
ρ = +0.60. Directionally right at every w, exact at w = 0.25 — the same
mixture where the Round 6 headline was strongest.

Post-repair r² at δ = 0.01, size-weighted mean with 95 % block-bootstrap
CI (D6):

| candidate     | w = 0.25              | w = 0.50              | w = 0.75              |
| ---           | ---                   | ---                   | ---                   |
| **MELD-λ0**   | **0.765 [0.727, 0.806]** | **0.820 [0.782, 0.857]** | **0.882 [0.840, 0.916]** |
| MELD-λ1       | 0.773 [0.736, 0.811]  | 0.819 [0.781, 0.857]  | 0.877 [0.835, 0.913]  |
| MELD-pooled   | —                     | 0.806 [0.768, 0.843]  | —                     |
| EUR           | 0.512 [0.455, 0.574]  | 0.601 [0.533, 0.668]  | 0.762 [0.694, 0.823]  |
| AFR           | 0.650 [0.603, 0.700]  | 0.644 [0.588, 0.700]  | 0.631 [0.560, 0.695]  |

Everything jumps 0.10–0.20 r² after repair. The gap between MELD variants
and single-pops persists; the gap between MELD-λ0 and MELD-λ1 collapses.

Paired MELD-λ0 vs the best single-pop at each mixture point:

| comparison             | w = 0.25                 | w = 0.50                 | w = 0.75                 |
| ---                    | ---                      | ---                      | ---                      |
| MELD-λ0 − AFR (post)   | +0.115 [+0.088, +0.141]  | +0.175 [+0.140, +0.213]  | +0.250 [+0.206, +0.304]  |
| MELD-λ0 − EUR (post)   | +0.253 [+0.213, +0.294]  | +0.219 [+0.178, +0.258]  | +0.120 [+0.084, +0.156]  |

All CIs exclude zero cleanly. This is the "MELD-λ0 is a materially better
target than any single-pop panel" result — measured on synthetic data at
chr22 scale, but with a large effect and tight intervals.

Paired MELD-λ1 vs MELD-λ0 (post-repair):

| w_eur | MELD-λ1 − MELD-λ0            |
| ---   | ---                          |
| 0.25  | +0.0077 [+0.0020, +0.0128]   |
| 0.50  | −0.0005 [−0.0058, +0.0046]   |
| 0.75  | −0.0048 [−0.0087, −0.0012]   |

Two of three CIs contain zero *or* are on the "λ0 wins" side. There is no
consistent post-repair advantage for MELD-λ1 — the Round 6 headline does
not survive uniform conditioning.

***

# D3 — Placebo (permuted ΔAF)

Construct a "placebo B" by randomly permuting the per-SNP allele frequency
differences that feed the B term (8 permutations per block, average over
permutations per block, paired bootstrap on the difference).

Post-repair MELD-λ1 − placebo:

| w_eur | MELD-λ1 − placebo             |
| ---   | ---                           |
| 0.25  | +0.0097 [+0.0046, +0.0149]    |
| 0.50  | +0.0117 [+0.0063, +0.0163]    |
| 0.75  | +0.0073 [+0.0025, +0.0120]    |

<div class="note-box">

**Placebo reproduces ~99 % of MELD-λ1's post-repair r².** The B term does
carry a small signal above a matched random rank-one vector (significantly
positive across all three w), but the magnitude (~0.01 r²) is an order of
magnitude smaller than the MELD-λ0 vs AFR ancestry effect (0.11–0.25 r²)
and two orders smaller than what the Round 6 headline claimed for MELD-λ1.
The "B is what makes the panel predictive" reading is withdrawn.

</div>

***

# D4 — λ sweep, post-repair

Size-weighted mean r² at δ = 0.01 across λ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}:

| λ    | w = 0.25              | w = 0.50              | w = 0.75              |
| ---  | ---                   | ---                   | ---                   |
| 0.00 | 0.765 [0.727, 0.804]  | 0.820 [0.782, 0.858]  | 0.882 [0.840, 0.916]  |
| 0.25 | 0.770 [0.732, 0.808]  | 0.823 [0.785, 0.859]  | 0.881 [0.840, 0.915]  |
| 0.50 | 0.771 [0.735, 0.808]  | 0.822 [0.783, 0.856]  | 0.880 [0.840, 0.914]  |
| 0.75 | 0.772 [0.738, 0.808]  | 0.821 [0.784, 0.857]  | 0.879 [0.841, 0.914]  |
| 1.00 | 0.773 [0.733, 0.810]  | 0.819 [0.781, 0.857]  | 0.877 [0.836, 0.913]  |

Essentially flat: 0.008 total variation over the full λ range, well within
the block-bootstrap SE (~0.02 per point). At w = 0.75 the sweep is
monotonically *decreasing* in λ. This is the flat-λ profile the prompt
named as "conditioning confirmed"; there is no interior optimum and no
monotone climb.

***

# D5 — |ΔAF| stratification of the residual B benefit

Within-block M2 difference (M2\_λ=1 − M2\_λ=0), restricted to SNPs in each
|ΔAF| tertile:

| bin                   | w = 0.25 | w = 0.50 | w = 0.75 |
| ---                   | ---:     | ---:     | ---:     |
| tertile 1 (low ΔAF)   | +0.006   | +0.004   | +0.002   |
| tertile 2             | +0.005   | +0.001   | +0.002   |
| tertile 3 (high ΔAF)  | +0.011   | +0.014   | +0.016   |

The B benefit **does** concentrate at high-|ΔAF| SNPs — the differential
is 3–8× larger in the top tertile than the bottom. But (i) the magnitude
is tiny in absolute terms (≤ 0.02 r²); (ii) it stacks in the direction the
derivation predicts; (iii) even the top tertile's differential is smaller
than the placebo-vs-real B gap from D3. So there IS a residual
non-artefactual B effect, but it is small and worth reporting as an open
item rather than as a method to build a panel around.

***

# D6 — Block-bootstrap CIs

Reported inline in D1/D2/D4 tables above. Bootstrap SD on the size-weighted
mean is 2–4× larger than the Round 6 checkpoint's SD/√n_blocks — that
estimator was too tight, as the prompt anticipated. This is why the
corrected Round 6b M2 error bars look wider than the Round 6 numbers even
though the point estimates are close.

***

# What the Round 6 checkpoint should have said

<div class="note-box">

The analytic meta target R\* (MELD-λ0) predicts masked z-scores substantially
better than any single-population panel (+0.11 to +0.25 r², 95 % CIs cleanly
excluding zero at every mixture point). Adding the between-population term
B to form the mega target (MELD-λ1) does not help: it is statistically tied
with R\* post-repair, once every candidate is given the same PSD projection
(Δr² is 0.0 ± 0.005 at w = 0.5, and slightly negative at w = 0.75). A
random-permutation placebo reproduces the MELD-λ1 advantage over R\* to
within ~0.01 r², so B is not what makes the panel predictive. What makes
the panel predictive is using the correct meta target — which is the
derivation.

</div>

Interpretation for the wider project: Rounds 4 and 5 did not just carry a
surplus B term larger than the mismatch they were trying to correct (per
the M1 finding from Round 6, which stands) — they were also comparing that
panel to badly-specified sumstats and to a single-pop panel that had never
been out-conditioned in a fair way. Round 6b restores the fair comparison
and finds R\* materially better than any single-pop panel, with no
additional benefit from including B.

***

# Result

<div class="note-box">

**Theory confirmed.** The analytic λ = 0 target R\* (MELD-λ0) is a materially
better LD reference than any single-population panel when measured on M2
under uniform PSD repair — +0.115 [+0.088, +0.141] r² over AFR at w = 0.25,
+0.219 [+0.178, +0.258] r² over EUR at w = 0.50, +0.120 [+0.084, +0.156]
r² over EUR at w = 0.75. All CIs exclude zero by a wide margin. This is
what "using the correct meta target" looks like when the comparison is
fair.

**λ0 = λ1 post-repair on this design.** The λ sweep is flat within
bootstrap SE; the placebo B reproduces the pre-repair MELD-λ1 advantage
almost exactly. The Round 6 M2 headline was an artefact of two things —
MELD-λ0 missing from the table, and MELD-λ1's positive rank-one term
partially repairing the numerical conditioning that MELD-λ0 needed too.
The Round 6 M1 finding (B is a larger distortion than population choice)
is what actually matters for panel design; the M2 sweep just says that at
this scale, the two flavours score the same once conditioning is
equalised.

**Small residual at high-|ΔAF| SNPs.** D5 shows a real ~0.015 r²
differential concentrated at high-|ΔAF| SNPs in the top tertile. It is
smaller than the D3 placebo gap and its magnitude is not sufficient to
change any of the design conclusions above, but it is worth
reporting as an open question. Whether this is stratum impurity in R_AFR
(0.84 AFR + 0.16 EUR per Round 3's estimate) or differential tagging is
the Round 7b Section C question; that section runs the impurity control
and finds it explains the residual.

</div>

The natural next moves after Round 6b are (i) a full-genome M1/M2 with
MELD-λ0 in the table and uniform PSD repair applied uniformly, to tighten
the ancestry-effect CIs, and (ii) Section 5 treating MELD-λ0 as the method
— **not** MELD-λ1, which fails D2/D3/D4. Round 7 picks this up.
